desc:
A pivot of an array is a position p with 1 ≤ p ≤ n - 1 such that nums[0] + ... + nums[p-1] = nums[p] + ... + nums[n-1], i.e. the prefix before p and the suffix from p have the same sum.

You may replace at most one element of nums by the value k (or leave the array alone). Return the largest possible number of pivots.

nums = [2, -1, 2], k = 3
no change: pivots 0 (p=1: 2 vs 1, p=2: 1 vs 2)
change nums[0] to 3 -> [3, -1, 2]: p=2 gives 2 vs 2, so 1 pivot
answer = 1
hints: Trying every index and re-counting pivots takes O(n) per index, O(n2) in total. For a fixed position p, let diff[p] = prefixSum(p) - suffixSum(p); a pivot is just diff[p] = 0.

Changing nums[i] by delta = k - nums[i] shifts diff[p] by +delta for every split p > i (element in the left part) and by -delta for every split p ≤ i (element in the right part). Splits are affected on only two sides.

Store the diff values of the splits on each side of i in two hash counters. The pivots after changing index i number right[-delta] + left[delta]. Sweep i from left to right, moving split p = i from the right counter to the left one, and take the maximum together with the unchanged count.
editorial: Let pre[p] be the sum of the first p elements and diff[p] = pre[p] - (total - pre[p]) for p = 1..n-1. The array has as many pivots as there are zeros among the diff values.

Replace nums[i] by k and put delta = k - nums[i]. Splits p > i have element i in their left part: left grows by delta, the right is unchanged, so diff[p] + delta must be 0. Splits p ≤ i have it in their right part, so diff[p] - delta must be 0. The number of pivots after this change is therefore #{p > i : diff[p] = -delta} + #{p ≤ i : diff[p] = delta}.

Keep a counter right filled with all diffs and an empty counter left. For i = 0..n-1, first move diff[i] (if 1 ≤ i ≤ n-1) from right to left, then evaluate the formula in O(1). The answer is the maximum of that and the count with no change. Time O(n), space O(n). All intermediate values fit comfortably in 64-bit integers (and the sums stay within 109).
